line: - **write-product-log** Write the product log from the template; for an old project, write it from the README, open issues and old plans, and leave the history in version control.
note: The sentence 'what cannot be written yet follows the blank-page rule' is the blank-page line. overview#1 keeps the one-product-log rule.

line: - **blank-page** If the product and its Product Goal cannot be written yet, start from a design and let its conclusions fill the product log; link the design, never copy its log. → long/product-log-details.md
note: Long file: the six-row table (design log to product log), the IDEO methods alone not being enough, the stakeholder table written first because a design uses role cards from its first stage.

line: - **facts-then-questions** [sm] *Supplement.* Look up the facts yourself; put what the PO must decide into one numbered message, each question with a recommended answer.
note: Kept with its Supplement label: inferred by the assistant, never confirmed in practice. The PO decides whether it stays.

line: - **product-log-header** Keep the product statement in 1.1 and the Product Goal in 1.2, each in a one-row commitment table; the product log has no Now or Waiting for PO line, since it has no stage.
note: The optional vision line is dropped from the list (the template has it).

lines: - **dod-in-product-log** Keep the full Definition of Done in section 1.3; a Sprint chooses where to focus its checks, never which standards apply.
- **dod-standards** Write standards precisely and keep only requirements that hold across the product; item-specific or tentative ones go in the item's acceptance criteria.
where_else: The two definitions (Outcome Done, Output Done) are in plugins/ideo-scrum/skills/scrum-kernel/references/scrum-artifact-increment.md.

line: - **stakeholder-table** [sm] List stakeholders in section 2.1 as a short table, one row each; a Stakeholder subagent gets one row as its identity; if the table is empty, ask the PO who belongs in it.
- **architecture-map** Start section 2.2 with one Mermaid flowchart TD map: actors on top (AI roles included), the ending at the bottom, five to fifteen steps between.
note: The verifier found that steps/2-1 draws actors on the left and the ending on the right, so this line cannot just point there. 'Add a subsection only for a step that needs more words' is dropped as detail.

line: - **no-tbd** Turn an unclear point into an item; a Sprint or a design works it out.
- **no-technical-design** Keep technical design out of the product log: modules and interfaces are the Developer's and live in the Increment.
- **item-columns** An item has seven columns: #, Title, User story, Place, Status, Size, Notes; what goes in each, and the S, M, L sizes, are in the long file. → long/product-log-details.md
note: The table is kept word for word in the long file: the template has only the column names.

line: - **numbers-not-ranks** Number items only to count them, keeping every number unique; ranking is separate, and the PO does it when an order is needed.
- **items-with-sm** [sm,po] The PO decides the items together with the Scrum Master; at Planning the PO leads the selection, and the Scrum Master and Developer say when it is too much or too little.
note: A departure from the Scrum Guide (the Developers select the items); the departure is in the departures long file. The check when the rows are written is the sprint line select-items.

line: - **status-lives-here** Write an item's status in the product log only; a sprint log names items by number.
- **refine-in-sprint** Refine in the product log only to add detail; finish refinement in the sprint log's section 2.2; the product log has no refinement section.
note: Low confidence in the annotation: part of the original is signposting.

line: - **acceptance-written-once** Acceptance criteria already written in full in the product log are not repeated in the sprint log.
where_else: The seven steps themselves are in the sprint-refinement long file.

line: - **where-refined-content** Put refined content where it belongs: a split-off item is a new row, long design content goes in the architecture, short notes in Notes, large material in scrum/documents/.
- **fresh-at-review** At every Review, move done items to section 3.2 (one line each, with its source), send unfinished ones back to 3.1, and delete outdated text; keep no revision record.
note: 'Fresh means more than the items: the Review keeps the rest of scrum/ fresh too' goes with the Review rule in the sprint-closing long file.

line: - **product-log-changes** Write an item's change and its reason in its Notes, and a Product Goal change with its date and reason in section 1.2; the PO changes the Product Goal only on evidence against it.
note: overview#17 covers 'only the PO changes a commitment'; this line adds where the changes are written and the evidence condition.
